findings.description: The reports_archive bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or explicit private ACL is defined for this bucket, leaving it open to accidental public ACLs or bucket policies exposing report data.
The bucket does not configure a logging block, so unauthorized access to archived reports cannot be detected or traced.
Versioning is not enabled, so objects can be overwritten or deleted irreversibly (including by an attacker destroying evidence), and force_destroy = true compounds the risk of data loss.
The ledger_exports bucket holds financial ledger data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so data is not encrypted with a managed/customer key.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource restricts public ACLs or policies for this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose ledger exports publicly.
No logging block is configured, leaving access to sensitive ledger exports unaudited.
Versioning is not enabled on this financial data bucket, so deleted or tampered objects cannot be recovered and MFA-delete protections are unavailable.
The model_artifacts bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
There is no public access block for this bucket, allowing future public ACLs or policies to expose proprietary model artifacts.
The ops_runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive internal procedures and credentials and are stored unencrypted.
No logging block is configured for the runbooks bucket, so reads of sensitive operational documentation are not recorded.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block constrains public ACLs or bucket policies on this bucket.
The audit log bucket has no public access block; because it uses the log-delivery-write ACL, an additional misconfiguration could expose audit logs publicly.
The audit trail bucket itself is not configured with access logging, so tampering with or exfiltration of the audit logs would go unrecorded.

The vendor-roster.xlsx object is uploaded to a bucket with no default encryption and without specifying kms_key_id or server_side_encryption, so potentially sensitive vendor data is stored in plaintext.
